result.headline: Heading estimate disagrees with setpoint and velocity from t=38 s; roll/pitch loop tracks its setpoint with lag.
result.explanation: The yaw estimate disagrees with both the yaw setpoint and the velocity vector from 38.142 s. Roll follows its setpoint with a 0.959 s lag and the actuators respond. A heading-sensor or estimator fault leads; the data cannot confirm it.

evidence.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[yaw] followed its setpoint worse from t=45.234 to 67.838 s: typical |error| up to 167.997 deg against 65.478 over the whole recording
evidence.shows: Yaw tracking error is large and sustained from 45.234 s. At 59.31 s the estimate is -41.868 deg while the setpoint is 125 deg (cc_9).

evidence.quote: CHANGE vehicle.velocity[x] at t=46.627 s: 12.11 -> -9.1 m/s (step -21.21, 111.6x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: Velocity swings and the yaw estimate move together. At 38.142 s yaw, velocity x and velocity y left baseline first, before any actuator (cc_8).

evidence.quote: CHANGE vehicle.attitude[yaw] at t=71.95 s: -0.678 -> 84.606 deg (step 85.284, 166.5x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: The yaw estimate jumps by 85.284 deg in one step, repeated at 81.278 s and 104.603 s. This looks like an estimator or compass discontinuity, not physical rotation.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=0.614 s controller.event[mavros: Battery] mavros: Battery: WARN: Low voltage
evidence.shows: A low-voltage warning and a sensor-health error appear together at 0.614 s, with no later events. No voltage series exists to test it.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT vehicle.yaw_rate[yaw] = 0 for the whole recording (472 samples)
evidence.shows: Yaw rate and airspeed (line 27) are constant 0 for the whole recording. These channels are dead or unlogged, so yaw cannot be cross-checked against a rate.

checked.check: Earliest signals to leave baseline in the 38-50 s window
checked.result: Yaw and velocity x/y left baseline together at 38.142 s. Actuators ch3-5 followed at 39.167 s, the yaw setpoint at 43.925 s and throttle at 45.025 s.

checked.check: Roll setpoint against roll attitude over the whole recording
checked.result: Correlation is 0.852 and rises to 0.974 at a lag of 0.959 s. The large roll errors are mostly delay on steep setpoint steps, not a loss of control authority.

checked.check: Actuator response at the start (0-8 s)
checked.result: ch2 moves 1452 -> 1124 -> 1548 us and ch1 moves 1477 -> 1547 -> 1464 us as the setpoints change. Outputs are alive and responsive.

checked.check: Yaw estimate against yaw setpoint and velocity direction (40-75 s)
checked.result: At 59.31 s yaw is -41.868 deg and the setpoint is 125 deg. Velocity is (-7.75, 12.14) m/s, pointing back and to the right (x negative, y positive). That is my own reading and the frame is assumed. It fits the setpoint better than the yaw estimate.

effects.why: Large roll setpoint swings are probably the controller chasing a heading error, so a consequence.

next_action.action: Rotate powered vehicle on ground through known headings; log yaw estimate and throttle
next_action.why: Separates a compass or estimator heading fault from a controller problem. Also tests whether throttle current corrupts the compass.
how: Props off. Place the vehicle on a bench, powered from a good battery.
Rotate it to N, E, S, W using a handheld reference compass. Record the yaw estimate at each heading.
Repeat with the motors armed at idle and then at mid throttle. Record the yaw change.
Read the compass calibration, the mag and gyro health flags and any EKF/estimator status.
next_action.conditions: Props removed, battery charged. Magnetometer away from metal. Repeat at idle and mid throttle. Arming motors needs a qualified engineer's approval.
next_action.baseline: Reference compass headings. Yaw estimate in the first stretch of this flight, where yaw error is lower (line 82).

outcomes.label: Yaw wrong on bench, static
outcomes.means: The magnetometer, its calibration or the estimator is the fault. The controller is only reacting to it.
outcomes.then: Recalibrate or replace the compass, then replay the flight.

outcomes.label: Yaw correct static, shifts with throttle
outcomes.means: Current-induced magnetic interference or a power problem is distorting the heading.
outcomes.then: Check wiring and routing; compare battery voltage under load.

outcomes.label: Yaw correct in every state
outcomes.means: Heading sensing works on the bench. Look at the flight-time estimator fusion and the mission or setpoint logic.
outcomes.then: Request the raw sensor logs and the estimator's innovation data.
